title: Backend, APIs & Database Foundations
description: Learn client-server contracts, HTTP operations, server validation, identity and permissions, persistence, transactions, and failure handling.

lessons.title: Client-server architecture
lessons.principle: Clients request actions or data; servers enforce trusted rules and coordinate data or external systems.
lessons.practice: Draw the flow from task form to API to database and back.

lessons.title: Place responsibilities deliberately
lessons.principle: Frontend validation improves usability, but it does not prevent forged network requests.
lessons.practice: Repeat mandatory authorization and input validation on the server.

lessons.title: HTTP requests and responses
lessons.principle: An HTTP exchange has a method, URL, headers, optional body, status, and response representation.
lessons.practice: Identify GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, and commonly used 2xx/4xx/5xx categories.

lessons.title: Use meaningful statuses
lessons.principle: A missing task and a broken database are not equivalent failures.
lessons.practice: Return a suitable not-found response for unknown IDs and a server error for an unexpected outage.

lessons.title: API contracts
lessons.principle: API endpoints should define resource names, request schema, response schema, and error behavior.
lessons.practice: Write a create-task contract before asking AI to implement it.

lessons.title: Avoid accidental breaking changes
lessons.principle: Clients may rely on existing field names, types, and nullability.
lessons.practice: Add fields compatibly where possible and document any intentionally breaking version transition.

lessons.title: Server-side validation
lessons.principle: Every externally supplied value can be absent, malformed, duplicated, oversized, or malicious.
lessons.practice: Validate type, length, ownership, and allowed values before business logic executes.

lessons.title: Make validation errors actionable
lessons.principle: Silent coercion can corrupt data and leave users uncertain about the fix.
lessons.practice: Return structured field errors without exposing stack traces or sensitive internal details.

lessons.title: Authentication and authorization
lessons.principle: Authentication establishes an identity; authorization decides what that identity may do.
lessons.practice: Explain why knowing a task ID is not permission to edit that task.

lessons.title: Prevent cross-user access
lessons.principle: Checking ownership only in the frontend cannot stop direct API calls.
lessons.practice: Filter or check each read and mutation by authenticated user or tenant on the trusted backend.

lessons.title: Database records and queries
lessons.principle: A database persists entities with types, keys, and queryable relationships.
lessons.practice: Model users and tasks with a stable task ID and user ownership.

lessons.title: Keep database constraints as safeguards
lessons.principle: Application checks alone cannot reliably prevent duplicates or invalid references during concurrency.
lessons.practice: Add NOT NULL, unique, and foreign-key constraints that enforce true domain invariants.

lessons.title: CRUD and persistence
lessons.principle: Create, read, update, and delete operations should have explicit success and failure semantics.
lessons.practice: Implement task creation and retrieval before expanding to more mutations.

lessons.title: Avoid silent data loss
lessons.principle: Replacing an entire list from stale client state can overwrite a concurrent user's change.
lessons.practice: Use scoped record updates with appropriate concurrency protection rather than blind full-table replacement.

lessons.title: Transactions and consistency
lessons.principle: A transaction groups related database changes so they succeed or fail together where supported.
lessons.practice: Identify invariants needing atomic changes, such as a transfer between two balances.

lessons.title: Handle retries safely
lessons.principle: An operation retried after a timeout may already have committed.
lessons.practice: Use stable operation IDs or idempotency mechanisms for non-repeatable side effects.

lessons.title: Concurrency and asynchronous jobs
lessons.principle: Multiple requests may overlap; long-running work may require queues, timeouts, and durable tracking.
lessons.practice: Do not keep a request open merely to wait for a lengthy report generation when a job model fits.

lessons.title: Define job status and ownership
lessons.principle: Background work needs explicit progress, retry, failure, and access rules.
lessons.practice: Store job IDs, enforce requester authorization, and avoid retrying non-idempotent actions blindly.

lessons.title: Resilience and observability
lessons.principle: Servers need informative logs, health checks, capacity limits, backups, and recoverable errors.
lessons.practice: Log a request identifier without logging passwords, tokens, or private payloads.

lessons.title: Test dependency failures
lessons.principle: A service must behave deliberately when its database or external API is unavailable.
lessons.practice: Simulate a database outage and verify response status, safe message, retry policy, and recovery.

codeExamples.snippet:
POST /api/tasks HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>

{"title":"Read requirements"}

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"task-123","title":"Read requirements","done":false}

CREATE TABLE tasks (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  owner_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(title)) > 0),
  done BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE
);
-- Server queries must also restrict owner_id.
